cell_type.evidence: In differentiated macrophage-like monocytic cells, we classified sets of both shared and distinct ISG proteins responsive to each IFN class.

Subsequent comparison of macrophage-like monocytic cells to primary keratinocytes enabled us to identify relative ISG abundances, cytokine induction, and antiviral capacities of both cell types across infections with several ubiquitous human viruses.

disease_state.evidence: inferred: We compared the effects of IFN classes on the cellular proteome and relative restriction of virus progeny production across multiple physiologically relevant cell types and viruses.
